meta.title: Peptide Reference
meta.source: Peptide Protocol Quick Reference v2.0 (primary) and Educational Master Reference v2.0 (mechanism language, cautions)
meta.disclaimer: Educational and research reference only. Not medical advice. None of these compounds are a substitute for licensed clinical care. Peptide and supplement protocols carry real risks, including injection-site reactions, hormonal disruption, receptor desensitization, drug interactions, and unknown long-term effects. Tesamorelin (Egrifta) is FDA-approved for HIV-associated lipodystrophy; Thymosin Alpha-1 (Zadaxin) is approved in 30+ countries. Most other entries are research-use compounds. Consult a qualified healthcare provider before initiating any protocol.

peptides.name: Retatrutide
peptides.cardDescription: A triple-pathway metabolic compound studied for appetite regulation, blood-sugar handling, and energy use. Think of it as a traffic controller that slows incoming calories while helping the body route fuel more efficiently.
peptides.bottomLine: Fewer calories in, better fuel use, and stronger metabolic signaling.
peptides.dose: 0.5–12 mg SQ weekly. Typical maintenance sits around 0.5–2 mg; active dosing runs 2–6 mg; escalate toward the 12 mg ceiling only when results actually call for it, titrating slowly given the ~6-day half-life.
peptides.halfLife: ~6 days
peptides.timing: Any time; fasted not required. Consistency matters more than the clock. Never skip the weekly dose.
peptides.cycling: Continuous weekly exposure in human trials; no receptor-reset cycle is established. Stopping is a separate decision from cycling and can allow the metabolic pressures being treated to return.
peptides.mechanism: Triple agonist. GLP-1 flips the hypothalamic hunger switch (POMC) and improves glucose-dependent insulin release. GIP makes fat tissue more insulin-sensitive. Glucagon turns on AMPK in the liver, shutting down new fat-making and ramping up fat-burning — up to 82% liver-fat reduction in Phase 2 trials. The 6-day half-life means each dose stacks on the last, so titration is not optional.
cautions: No established biological cycling requirement — this is studied as continuous therapy, not an on/off protocol. Stopping is a separate decision that can let the underlying metabolic pressures return.
Titrate slowly. A 6-day half-life accumulates; jumping straight to maintenance raises GI side effects.
Missed doses cause more fluctuation than with shorter-acting compounds given the 6-day half-life — consistency matters more than perfect timing.

Tingling/altered skin sensation and gallbladder issues (gallstones, occasionally inflammation) have both shown up with this compound — generally mild, dose-related, and worth knowing about rather than being alarmed by.

peptides.name: MOTS-C
peptides.cardDescription: A mitochondrial signaling peptide studied for helping muscle cells take up glucose and respond more efficiently during metabolic stress. Think of it as a thermostat message telling the cell’s power system to use fuel more effectively.
peptides.bottomLine: Helps cells handle fuel with less metabolic strain.
peptides.halfLife: 30–60 min plasma; signaling effects persist 24–48 hrs
peptides.timing: Fasted; at least 2 hours after a meal. Pre-workout or bedtime.
peptides.cycling: 8–12 weeks on, 4 months off. Maximum 3 cycles per year.
peptides.mechanism: A 16-amino-acid mitochondrial peptide — the exercise mimetic. It inhibits the folate cycle so AICAR builds up, AMPK turns on, and GLUT4 moves to the muscle-cell surface. Glucose walks in without needing insulin. Under metabolic stress it also travels to the nucleus and reprograms metabolic gene expression.
cautions: Maximum 3 cycles per year — this is a reprogramming signal, not a daily vitamin.
Inject fasted or more than 2 hours after a meal.
Tissue signaling lasts 24–48 hours; more frequent dosing is not automatically better.
supplements: Berberine 500 mg 3×/day (additive AMPK: MOTS-C via folate cycle, berberine via Complex I)
ALA 600 mg/day (reduces ROS that impairs GLUT4)

peptides.name: 5-Amino-1MQ
peptides.cardDescription: A research small molecule—not a peptide—studied for blocking an enzyme that drains NAD+ inside fat cells. Think of it as plugging an energy leak so more cellular fuel remains available for metabolic work.
peptides.bottomLine: Preserves cellular fuel by blocking a major NAD+ drain.
peptides.halfLife: 4–6 hours
peptides.timing: Morning with food.
peptides.cycling: 8 weeks on, 4 weeks off.
peptides.mechanism: Blocks NNMT — the enzyme in white fat that steals NAD+ and burns through SAM. Preserving NAD+ inside fat cells turns on SIRT1 and AMPK, which flip thermogenic genes (UCP1, PGC-1α). White fat “browns” and energy expenditure rises. Pairing with NMN adds NAD+ substrate while 5-Amino-1MQ stops the leak.
cautions: Cycle 8 weeks on / 4 weeks off.
This is a small-molecule NNMT inhibitor, not a classic peptide — still research-use.
Take in the morning with food.
supplements: NAD+/NMN 500 mg–1 g fasted AM (blocks the leak + adds substrate)
Resveratrol 500 mg/day with food (SIRT1 activator synergy)

peptides.name: KPV
peptides.cardDescription: A three-amino-acid fragment studied for calming inflammatory signaling, especially around the gut. Think of it as a fire extinguisher that quiets the alarm before repair work begins.
peptides.bottomLine: Calms inflammatory signaling so healing has a quieter environment.
peptides.dose: 250–500 mcg SQ daily. Oral 500 mcg–1 mg for gut-specific targeting.
peptides.halfLife: 1–2 hrs plasma; PepT1 uptake extends tissue effect
peptides.timing: Injectable: anytime. Oral: empty stomach for gut-lining delivery.
peptides.cycling: 8–12 weeks on, 4 weeks off. PRN for acute flares.
peptides.mechanism: THE FIRE EXTINGUISHER. Rides the PepT1 transporter (very high affinity) and concentrates at inflamed sites. Inside the cell it physically blocks importin-α3 from carrying p65RelA into the nucleus — so NF-κB cannot write TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-6, or IL-8. Also taps MC1R/MC3R (cAMP) and quiets MAPK. Put the fire out before the construction crew arrives.
cautions: Oral only works well on an empty stomach if the goal is gut delivery.
For chronic use, take a 4-week break after 8–12 weeks.
Does not add the pigmentation effects of full alpha-MSH.
supplements: Curcumin 500–1000 mg 2–3×/day liposomal (NF-κB via a different binding site)

peptides.name: Alpha-MSH
peptides.cardDescription: The parent hormone from which KPV is derived, studied for wider anti-inflammatory signaling throughout the body and brain. Think of it as a whole-building sprinkler system rather than one handheld extinguisher.
peptides.bottomLine: Broadens inflammatory control beyond the more focused KPV signal.
peptides.halfLife: ~30 min plasma; receptor effects last hours
peptides.timing: Fasted preferred.
peptides.cycling: 4–6 weeks on, 4 weeks off. Monitor pigmentation.
peptides.mechanism: The full parent of KPV. Activates MC1R, MC3R, MC4R, and MC5R → cAMP → PKA → IκBα stays phosphorylated so NF-κB is locked in the cytoplasm. MC4R adds central (hypothalamic) anti-inflammatory control that KPV cannot reach. Lowers TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-6, IL-17, and IFN-γ and raises IL-10. Broader spectrum than KPV.
cautions: Monitor skin pigmentation with prolonged use.
Cycle 4–6 weeks on / 4 weeks off to limit receptor desensitization.
Use when the goal is systemic and central immune modulation; use KPV when the goal is gut-specific NF-κB shutdown.

peptides.name: ARA-290
peptides.cardDescription: An EPO-derived research peptide designed to activate repair pathways without stimulating red-blood-cell production. Think of it as an injury beacon that helps protect stressed nerves and may turn down pain signaling.
peptides.bottomLine: Signals protection and repair where nerves are under stress.
peptides.halfLife: Short (hours)
peptides.timing: Timing-independent.
peptides.cycling: 28-day cycles; repeatable.
peptides.mechanism: An 11-amino-acid EPO fragment that turns on the Innate Repair Receptor (EPOR + CD131), which is upregulated at injury sites. That fires PI3K/Akt and JAK2/STAT3 — anti-apoptotic, anti-inflammatory, pro-survival. Separately it raises the TRPV1 pain-channel threshold, which is why neuropathic pain can ease. Promotes nerve-fiber regrowth. No red-blood-cell stimulation.
cautions: Does not stimulate red blood cells — that is the point versus EPO.
Short plasma life; tissue repair signaling is what you are dosing for.
Typically run as 28-day cycles.

peptides.name: BPC-157
peptides.cardDescription: Think of it as the construction foreman for injured tissue — it doesn't build anything itself. It gets your body's repair crews to the site faster and keeps them working in an organized way instead of leaving a mess. Mostly used for joints, tendons, and gut healing; nerve, spinal-cord, and heart-protection findings are mostly animal studies.
peptides.bottomLine: Repair coordinator, not the building material. The same blood-vessel growth that helps healing is why active or recent cancer history is not a casual reach.
peptides.dose: 0.25–1 mg SQ daily typical (often 250–500 mcg, split AM/PM). Trial-scaled ~100–110 mcg/day; practical range is 2–5× that. Up to 2 mg short-term for severe acute injury; diminishing returns above 1 mg. Oral 250–500 mcg is a gut-local option, not a proven systemic route.
peptides.halfLife: ~15 min plasma; downstream repair signaling lasts 24h+. Gut-stable; systemic oral absorption uncharacterized.
peptides.timing: Injectable once daily or split AM/PM ~12h apart. Oral: gut-local only.
peptides.cycling: No evidence of tolerance/downregulation with continuous use — no receptor has been identified to test that. 8–12 week runs track structural repair better than the shorter 4–6 week convention. Stopping is a separate decision from cycling.
peptides.mechanism: Turns on blood-vessel growth two ways (VEGFR2 + eNOS release) and flips EGR-1 to pull repair cells in. Resolves inflammation rather than blocking it. Organ-system signals (preclinical unless noted): cardiac infarct models; stroke ischemia models; spinal-cord compression; strongest independent evidence in tendon/ligament; bone defects; kidney and distant-organ protection; gut lining (deepest evidence, only system with human-trial history); lung-injury models (COVID-specific claims are hypothesis); serotonin-linked antidepressant-like models; metabolic insulin-sensitivity is reasoned extrapolation. Same angiogenesis mechanism is the cancer caution.
cautions: Genuinely unresolved in cancer: the same blood-vessel-growth mechanism behind healing is what oncology drugs block in existing tumors. No study either direction. Not a casual reach with active or recent cancer history.
Most organ-system findings are animal work, concentrated in one research group. Independent tendon/angiogenesis papers exist; they do not convert rodent outcomes into human protocols.
Feeling better can arrive before tissue is structurally ready.
WADA-prohibited (S0). Not FDA-compoundable as of Aug 2026 — July 2026 advisory vote to reverse, not yet enacted.

peptides.name: TB-500
peptides.cardDescription: A thymosin beta-4 fragment studied for helping repair cells move through the body toward injured tissue. Think of it as dispatch sending mobile crews to multiple job sites rather than managing one local repair.
peptides.bottomLine: Mobilizes repair activity across the body.
peptides.dose: Loading: 4–6 mg/week for 6 weeks (2–3 injections). Maintenance: 2–2.5 mg/week.
peptides.halfLife: <2 hrs plasma; tissue effects last days to weeks
peptides.timing: Anytime; food-independent.
peptides.cycling: 6-week loading, then maintenance, or 8–12 week cycles.
peptides.mechanism: THE SYSTEMIC MOBILIZER. A synthetic Thymosin β4 fragment that binds G-actin and resets the G-actin/F-actin equilibrium. Repair cells — immune, endothelial, progenitor — become highly motile and migrate rapidly to every injury site. Directly upregulates VEGF in poorly vascularized tissue and shifts macrophages from M1 (damage) to M2 (repair).
cautions: This is a whole-body mobilizer, not a local construction signal like BPC-157.
Load, then drop to a maintenance dose — do not stay at loading dose indefinitely.
Food does not change absorption.
supplements: Vitamin C 2–5 g/day (collagen for the cells TB-500 mobilizes)
Omega-3 2–4 g EPA/DHA (membranes of mobilized cells)
Magnesium glycinate 400 mg (muscle recovery; less tension at repair sites)
Zinc 25–50 mg/day with food (wound healing + collagen cofactor)

peptides.name: GHK-Cu
peptides.cardDescription: A naturally occurring copper peptide studied for collagen production, scar remodeling, skin quality, and tissue renewal. Think of it as a renovation manager that removes damaged material while directing a cleaner rebuild.
peptides.bottomLine: Supports the replacement and remodeling of worn or damaged tissue.
peptides.dose: 1 mg/day SQ on days 1–15; 2 mg/day SQ on days 16–30. Topical 2×/day. Maintenance: 1–2 mg SQ 2–3×/week.
peptides.halfLife: 0.5–2 hrs plasma
peptides.timing: Anytime. Topical: apply 2×/day.
peptides.cycling: Why cycle: copper accumulation (systemic copper/ceruloplasmin load) plus diminishing return once the remodeling gene program is already upregulated — not classic receptor desensitization. Injectable 1–2 mg SC 2–3×/week: 4–8 weeks on, 2–4 weeks off. Topical: can run 8–12 weeks continuously with periodic 2–4 week breaks because systemic copper load is minimal. Chronic or repeated cycles: check copper status before extending rather than running blind. If long-term, monitor serum copper, ceruloplasmin, and zinc (copper antagonizes zinc). Common pairing: BPC-157, with aligned cycle windows.
peptides.mechanism: BIOLOGICAL GENOME RESET. An endogenous copper-carrying tripeptide that modulates 4,000+ genes (Pickart et al., PMID 26236730). Increases type I/III collagen synthesis and glycosaminoglycan content, and modulates MMP activity via TIMP-1/2 to balance breakdown and rebuild (Maquart et al., PMID 8227353). Separately reduces TNF-α-induced IL-6 secretion — an anti-inflammatory action, not routed through TIMP1/2. Chemoattracts and activates mast cells as part of orchestrating the wound-to-remodeling transition (Zetter et al. PMID 3162062; Pickart PMID 18644225) — not a mast-cell-stabilizing/histamine-suppressing action. Delivers copper to lysyl oxidase and other copper-dependent enzymes involved in collagen cross-linking (mechanistically plausible; not directly demonstrated for GHK-Cu specifically).
cautions: Contraindicated in Wilson’s disease (copper-carrying peptide).
Cycle because of copper load and diminishing remodeling return, not because of classic receptor desensitization.
Injectable 1–2 mg SC 2–3×/week: 4–8 weeks on, 2–4 weeks off. Do not extend blindly.
Topical can run 8–12 weeks with a 2–4 week break; systemic copper load is much lower.
If using long-term or repeating cycles, check serum copper, ceruloplasmin, and zinc first — copper can silently lower zinc.
New collagen still needs vitamin C and silica to be structurally sound.
supplements: Silica 10–30 mg (collagen crosslinking at the same ECM level)
Resveratrol 500 mg (SIRT1 amplifies GHK-Cu gene effects)

peptides.name: CEPO
peptides.cardDescription: An investigational form of EPO redesigned to emphasize tissue protection without increasing red-blood-cell production. Think of it as a longer-duration survival signal for vulnerable nerve cells.
peptides.bottomLine: A research-stage signal aimed at sustained neuroprotection.
peptides.dose: Research phase — protocols not yet standardized for human use.
peptides.halfLife: Extended versus ARA-290
peptides.timing: Injectable; timing-independent.
peptides.cycling: Research protocols only.
peptides.mechanism: Carbamylated EPO that cannot form the EPOR2 homodimer, so it does not stimulate red blood cells. It selectively activates the Innate Repair Receptor (EPOR + CD131) and the CD131/GDNF/AKT path — GDNF being one of the strongest neuronal survival signals known. Protects hippocampal neurons from amyloid-beta in Alzheimer’s models. Longer duration than ARA-290; a chronic neuroprotection specialist.
cautions: Research-phase compound — human dosing is not standardized.
No red-blood-cell stimulation (by design).
Treat as investigational; not a drop-in substitute for ARA-290 without clinician oversight.
supplements: ALA 600–1200 mg/day (blood–brain antioxidant for the neurons CEPO protects)

peptides.name: SS-31
peptides.cardDescription: A mitochondria-targeted peptide studied for stabilizing cardiolipin, which helps the inner mitochondrial membrane and energy chain hold their shape. Think of it as reinforcing the power plant’s wiring before energy leaks away.
peptides.bottomLine: Protects mitochondrial structure so energy production can run more cleanly.
peptides.halfLife: Short plasma; mitochondrial accumulation via charge gradient
peptides.timing: Anytime.
peptides.cycling: 8–12 weeks on, 4 weeks off.
peptides.mechanism: A cationic peptide that accumulates in the inner mitochondrial membrane and binds cardiolipin — the phospholipid that holds cristae and the electron-transport chain together. By stopping ROS from oxidizing cardiolipin, Complex I and IV stay assembled. Electron leak falls at the source. Result: more ATP and less ROS at the same time. Not an antioxidant scavenger — a structural stabilizer. In clinical trials for heart failure.
cautions: Short plasma half-life; the useful effect is mitochondrial accumulation.
This is complementary to CoQ10, not a replacement for it.
Cycle 8–12 weeks on / 4 weeks off in the source protocol.
supplements: CoQ10 200–400 mg with MCT (ETC carrier at Complex I–III)
Glutathione liposomal 500–1000 mg (master antioxidant at the IMM)
ALA 600 mg (mito-specific antioxidant; regenerates C, E, glutathione)
Benfotiamine 150–300 mg (PDH/KGDH cofactor feeding Krebs → ETC)

peptides.name: Epitalon
peptides.cardDescription: A short pineal peptide studied for effects on melatonin rhythms, cellular-aging pathways, and DNA protection. Think of it as a periodic clock-reset signal rather than a compound intended for continuous use.
peptides.bottomLine: A cycle-based signal aimed at sleep timing and cellular maintenance.
peptides.dose: 5–10 mg SQ daily for 10 days; 2–4 cycles per year.
peptides.halfLife: Short plasma; epigenetic effects persist months
peptides.timing: Evening preferred.
peptides.cycling: 10-day cycles, 2–4×/year. Never continuous — receptor effects require rest.
peptides.mechanism: A pineal tetrapeptide from the Khavinson protocol. Activates telomerase, adding protective caps to chromosome ends — the primary cellular-aging clock. Restores pineal melatonin (which falls ~80% by age 70); melatonin itself is a potent mitochondrial antioxidant. Raises SOD and catalase, normalizes cortisol/LH/FSH/thyroid, and upregulates DNA-repair genes.
cautions: Never use continuously. Receptor effects require rest between 10-day courses.
2–4 cycles per year is the ceiling in the source protocol.
Evening dosing aligns with the pineal/melatonin restoration story.
supplements: Melatonin 0.5–3 mg bedtime (replaces what Epitalon is asking the pineal to make)
Magnesium glycinate 400 mg bedtime (sleep quality + melatonin-receptor sensitivity)
Resveratrol 500 mg/day (SIRT1 complements Epitalon’s gene effects)
CoQ10 200–400 mg (mito support alongside melatonin restoration)

peptides.name: Humanin
peptides.cardDescription: A mitochondria-derived peptide studied for helping stressed cells resist premature self-destruction, particularly in nervous tissue. Think of it as an emergency brake on the cellular shutdown sequence.
peptides.bottomLine: Helps vulnerable cells stay alive long enough to recover.
peptides.halfLife: Short plasma
peptides.timing: Anytime.
peptides.cycling: 8 weeks on, 4 weeks off.
peptides.mechanism: Encoded in the 16S rRNA of the mitochondrial genome — the second major mito-derived peptide family after MOTS-C. Directly binds BAX so it cannot oligomerize in the outer membrane. No cytochrome c release, no apoptosis cascade. Also protects neurons from amyloid-beta (circulating Humanin inversely tracks Alzheimer’s risk) and activates STAT3 + AMPK for better insulin sensitivity. Levels fall with age.
cautions: This is a cytoprotective / anti-apoptotic signal, not a stimulant.
Cycle 8 weeks on / 4 weeks off.
Circulating levels decline with age — that is part of the rationale, not a dosing instruction.
supplements: CoQ10 200–400 mg (protects the IMM from the oxidative stress that activates BAX)
ALA 600 mg (reduces ROS signals that activate BAX)
Lion’s Mane 500–1000 mg (NGF alongside Humanin’s neuroprotection)

peptides.name: NAD+
peptides.cardDescription: A coenzyme—not a peptide—required for energy production, sirtuin activity, and DNA repair. Think of it as the rechargeable electron carrier that keeps the cell’s power and maintenance systems moving.
peptides.bottomLine: Carries energy and supports enzymes involved in cellular maintenance.
peptides.dose: NMN/NR: 500 mg–1 g oral, fasted AM. Injectable: 100–500 mg IV/SQ.
peptides.halfLife: Rapid cellular turnover; precursors raise levels over days
peptides.timing: Precursors: fasted morning. Injectable: anytime.
peptides.cycling: Continuous maintenance. Optional quarterly loading cycles.
peptides.mechanism: Required for 500+ enzymatic reactions. Primary electron carrier from glycolysis and the Krebs cycle into Complex I (as NADH) — without it the ETC stalls. Fuel for sirtuins (SIRT1–7): gene expression, mitochondrial biogenesis (PGC-1α), DNA repair (SIRT6). PARP-1 also consumes NAD+; chronic inflammation hyperactivates PARP and drains the pool. NAD+ falls ~50% between ages 40 and 60.
cautions: Oral NMN/NR are precursors; they are not identical to IV/SQ NAD+.
Inflammation (PARP over-activation) can burn through what you supplement.
Pairing with 5-Amino-1MQ addresses the demand-side leak in fat tissue.
supplements: 5-Amino-1MQ 50–100 mg AM (blocks NAD+ depletion in fat cells)
ALA 600 mg (regenerates NAD+ from NADH in some reactions)

peptides.name: Methylene Blue
peptides.cardDescription: A drug—not a peptide—studied for carrying electrons around damaged sections of the mitochondrial energy chain at carefully controlled doses. Think of it as a temporary detour that keeps traffic moving when part of the power route is blocked.
peptides.bottomLine: Creates an alternate route for mitochondrial energy flow.
peptides.halfLife: ~5–6 hrs; urinary excretion (blue urine is expected)
peptides.timing: Morning with food. High doses inhibit the ETC.
peptides.cycling: 5 days on / 2 days off, or continuous at a low dose.
peptides.mechanism: UNIQUE: accepts electrons from NADH/FADH2 and donates them directly to cytochrome c, bypassing Complexes I, II, and III. ATP can still be made at Complex IV when those complexes are damaged. Third leg of the fatigue stack — MOTS-C gets glucose in, retatrutide fixes metabolic signaling, methylene blue lets mitochondria actually use that glucose. Raises Complex IV activity in neurons. Hormetic: above ~4–10 mg/kg it paradoxically inhibits.
cautions: Pharmaceutical grade only. Industrial or lab grade contains impurities that do not belong in a body.
Hormetic window: 0.5–4 mg/kg helps; high doses inhibit the electron-transport chain. More is not better.
Blue/green urine is expected, not a toxicity signal by itself.
Morning dosing. Discuss MAOI / serotonergic drug interactions with a clinician — methylene blue is a monoamine oxidase inhibitor at relevant doses.
supplements: CoQ10 200–400 mg (covers Complex I–III alongside the bypass)
ALA 600 mg (mito antioxidant; synergistic with MB redox cycling)
Benfotiamine 150–300 mg (feeds acetyl-CoA → Krebs → NADH → MB system)
NAC 600–1200 mg (raises glutathione; works with MB’s antioxidant action)

peptides.name: CJC-1295 (with DAC)
peptides.cardDescription: A long-acting GHRH analog studied for extending the duration of the body’s own pulsatile growth-hormone release. Think of it as keeping the pituitary’s signal window open longer.
peptides.bottomLine: Extends the growth-hormone signal while preserving a pulse-based pattern.
peptides.halfLife: 6–8 days (DAC binds albumin)
peptides.timing: Bedtime, fasted (2+ hours after a meal). No food for 30–60 min after injection. If using evening progesterone, shift to morning.
peptides.cycling: 12 weeks on, 4 weeks off.
peptides.mechanism: A GHRH(1–29) analog with four amino-acid substitutions plus DAC, which sticks the peptide to albumin and stretches the half-life from minutes to 6–8 days. Binds GHRH receptors on pituitary somatotrophs and stimulates pulsatile GH — the natural pattern, not a flat exogenous-HGH wave. One injection can keep GH 2–10× for ~6 days and IGF-1 1.5–3× for 9–11 days; repeated dosing can hold IGF-1 up for 28+ days. Bedtime dosing rides the largest natural slow-wave GH pulse.
cautions: Cycle 12 weeks on / 4 weeks off to limit pituitary receptor desensitization.
Must be fasted. Food after injection blunts the GH pulse — wait 30–60 minutes.
If evening progesterone is in use, move the injection to morning.
This is duration. Pair with Ipamorelin if the goal is duration plus amplitude.
supplements: Zinc 25–50 mg/day with food (pituitary GH-synthesis cofactor)
Vitamin D3/K2 10,000 IU + 200 mcg (pituitary D receptors influence GH)
Glycine 3 g bedtime (slow-wave sleep + natural GH pulse)
Magnesium glycinate 400 mg bedtime (sleep depth + GH signaling)
Melatonin 0.5–3 mg bedtime (sleep onset for the GH pulse)
Vitamin C 2 g/day (collagen driven by elevated IGF-1)
Ashwagandha 300–600 mg evening (lowers cortisol that opposes GH)

peptides.name: Ipamorelin
peptides.cardDescription: A selective ghrelin-receptor agonist studied for increasing the strength of natural growth-hormone pulses. Think of it as turning up the volume of a pulse rather than lengthening the song.
peptides.bottomLine: Strengthens pulse amplitude while CJC supplies additional duration.
peptides.halfLife: ~2 hours
peptides.timing: Bedtime, strictly fasted (primary). Optional AM fasted dose. Food blunts the GH pulse — wait 30–60 min before eating.
peptides.cycling: 12 weeks on, 4 weeks off.
peptides.mechanism: A synthetic ghrelin analog. Activates GHS-R1a on pituitary somatotrophs and amplifies GH pulse strength (amplitude). Selective: no cortisol or prolactin spike — that is what separates it from GHRP-2, GHRP-6, and hexarelin. Partially overrides somatostatin via the ghrelin path. Synergy with CJC-1295: CJC is duration, Ipamorelin is amplitude. Together they maximize GH while keeping the pulsatile pattern.
cautions: Strictly fasted. Food blunts the GH pulse.
Wait 30–60 minutes after injection before eating.
Cycle 12 / 4 to protect receptor sensitivity.
Does not replace sleep — the bedtime pulse is the main event.
supplements: Ashwagandha 300–600 mg evening (cortisol reduction amplifies GH)
Collagen peptides 10–20 g (raw material for IGF-1-driven repair)

peptides.name: Tesamorelin
peptides.cardDescription: A prescription GHRH analog approved for reducing excess abdominal fat in adults with HIV-associated lipodystrophy. It is studied through its effects on growth hormone and IGF-1, with a particular focus on deep abdominal fat.
peptides.bottomLine: A clinically established GHRH signal with visceral-fat specificity.
peptides.halfLife: ~26 min (daily dosing required)
peptides.timing: Bedtime, fasted.
peptides.cycling: 12 weeks on, 4 weeks off. FDA-approved for continuous use in HIV-associated lipodystrophy.
peptides.mechanism: The FDA-approved GHRH analog (Egrifta) — strongest published clinical safety data of any GHRH analog here. Same pituitary GHRHR mechanism as CJC-1295, but without DAC, so you dose every night. Visceral-fat specificity: GH receptors on intra-abdominal adipocytes preferentially drive lipolysis in the most metabolically dangerous depot. Raises IGF-1, which supports muscle and bone while that visceral fat comes off.
cautions: Daily dosing is required — the half-life is ~26 minutes.
FDA-approved indication is HIV-associated lipodystrophy; other uses are off-label.
Bedtime and fasted, same logic as the other GHRH analogs.
Practical research cycles are often 12 weeks on / 4 weeks off.
supplements: Berberine 500 mg 3×/day (complementary visceral-fat reduction via AMPK)
Vitamin D3/K2 10,000 IU + 200 mcg (D deficiency worsens visceral adiposity)
Glycine 3 g bedtime (sleep + natural GH-pulse synergy)

peptides.name: AOD-9604
peptides.cardDescription: A modified fragment of human growth hormone studied for fat breakdown without the broader growth effects of full HGH. Think of it as isolating the fat-mobilizing instruction from the larger hormone message.
peptides.bottomLine: Targets the fat-metabolism portion of the HGH signal.
peptides.halfLife: ~30 min
peptides.timing: Morning, fasted, 30 min before the first meal. Insulin blocks the lipolytic action.
peptides.cycling: 12 weeks on, 4 weeks off.
peptides.mechanism: HGH fragment 176–191 with an N-terminal tyrosine. Keeps HGH’s fat-metabolism program without anabolic effects, IGF-1 rise, or diabetogenic risk. Activates beta-3 adrenergic receptors in adipose tissue → lipolysis, fatty-acid mobilization, thermogenesis. Inhibits pre-adipocyte differentiation (fewer new fat cells). Emerging data on cartilage regeneration.
cautions: Must be morning and fasted. Insulin blocks the lipolytic action — do not pair with a carb-heavy breakfast.
Wait 30 minutes before the first meal.
This is not anabolic HGH and will not raise IGF-1 like a secretagogue stack.
supplements: ALA 600 mg/day (fatty-acid metabolism + ROS from increased lipolysis)
L-carnitine 1–2 g AM (shuttles mobilized fatty acids into mitochondria)
CoQ10 200–400 mg (ETC for burning the fat AOD-9604 releases)

peptides.name: Semax
peptides.cardDescription: An intranasal ACTH-fragment analog studied for BDNF and NGF signaling, attention, and neural recovery. Think of it as turning up the brain’s growth-and-repair instructions during periods of cognitive demand.
peptides.bottomLine: Supports signals involved in focus, plasticity, and neural repair.
peptides.halfLife: Minutes in plasma; CNS effects last hours via BDNF
peptides.timing: Morning preferred. Intranasal olfactory route bypasses the blood–brain barrier.
peptides.cycling: 2 weeks on / 2 weeks off. Not for chronic continuous use.
peptides.mechanism: An ACTH(4–10) heptapeptide analog. The nose-to-brain route skips the blood–brain barrier. Primary job: dramatically upregulate BDNF (survival, dendrites, synaptic plasticity, neurogenesis) and NGF (central and peripheral neural repair). Also lifts serotonergic and dopaminergic tone, protects against ischemia and oxidative stress, and raises antioxidant enzymes in brain tissue. Used clinically in Russia for stroke recovery and TBI rehab.
cautions: Not for chronic continuous use — 2 weeks on / 2 weeks off.
Morning preferred; this is a neurotrophic stimulant, not a night peptide.
Intranasal technique matters — this is an olfactory BBB bypass, not a gut peptide.
supplements: Lion’s Mane 500–1000 mg/day dual extract (NGF via hericenones/erinacines)
Omega-3 DHA 2–3 g/day (neuronal membrane fat for BDNF-driven synapses)
Magnesium threonate 2 g/day (brain Mg for NMDA + synaptic plasticity)
Bacopa 300–450 mg with fat (BDNF + memory consolidation)
Glutathione liposomal 500–1000 mg (neuroinflammatory ROS depletes BDNF)

peptides.name: Selank
peptides.cardDescription: An intranasal tuftsin analog studied for modulating GABA-related calming pathways without acting like a conventional sedative. Think of it as lowering background alarm noise while leaving the mind awake.
peptides.bottomLine: Aims for calm clarity rather than sedation.
peptides.halfLife: Minutes in plasma; CNS effects last hours
peptides.timing: Morning, or PRN for anxiety. Intranasal delivery.
peptides.cycling: 2 weeks on / 2 weeks off, or acute PRN between cycles.
peptides.mechanism: A tuftsin hexapeptide analog. Modulates GABA-A — the same receptor family as benzodiazepines — without addiction, tolerance, or respiratory depression. Upregulates BDNF (additive with Semax). Inhibits enkephalinase, raising enkephalins for mood via the endogenous opioid system (no direct opioid agonism). Lowers CNS IL-6 and TNF-α and supports serotonergic transmission.
cautions: Anxiolytic, not sedating in the benzodiazepine sense — still respect cycling.
2 on / 2 off, or keep it PRN between cycles.
Magnesium deficiency undercuts the GABA-A story; the supportive stack is not optional if anxiety is the target.
supplements: Magnesium glycinate 400 mg/day (cortisol down + GABA-A sensitivity)
Lion’s Mane 500–1000 mg (NGF complements Selank’s neuroprotection)

peptides.name: Dihexa
peptides.cardDescription: A highly potent investigational compound studied for HGF and c-Met signaling and the formation of new synaptic connections. Think of it as an architect for neural wiring, intended only after metabolic and inflammatory foundations are addressed.
peptides.bottomLine: A powerful research compound aimed at rebuilding neural connections.
peptides.dose: 10–30 mg topical in DMSO, or 1–5 mg intranasal.
peptides.halfLife: Days (CNS persistence) — extremely potent
peptides.timing: Anytime. Sequence is the constraint, not the clock.
peptides.cycling: 4 weeks on / 4 weeks off. Strict, conservative cycling.
peptides.mechanism: NOT an entry-point peptide. Fix insulin resistance, inflammation, and mitochondria first — the operating system — then upgrade the hardware. Potentiates HGF/c-Met to drive synaptogenesis. About 10-million-fold more potent than BDNF for dendritic-spine formation in the cited models. Rebuilds synaptic architecture lost in neurodegeneration. Sequence-critical on purpose.
cautions: Sequence critical: not an entry-point peptide. Address metabolic, inflammatory, and mitochondrial foundations first.
Start at the lowest effective dose. Extraordinary potency.
Long-term continuous use is not recommended. 4 weeks on / 4 weeks off is mandatory in the source protocol.
You cannot build new synapses on a brain that is inflamed, energy-deficient, and glucose-dysregulated.
supplements: Bacopa 300–450 mg (cholinergic support for new synapses)

peptides.name: Adamax
peptides.cardDescription: A modified Semax-related research compound designed for stronger brain penetration and a longer BDNF signal. Think of it as Semax with a longer broadcast range and duration.
peptides.bottomLine: Extends the neuroplasticity signal, making timing and cycling important.
peptides.dose: 100–500 mcg intranasal. Start at 100 mcg; many settle at 200–300 mcg.
peptides.halfLife: ~90 min plasma; BDNF effects 12–24 hrs
peptides.timing: Morning only. Never after 1 PM or expect insomnia.
peptides.cycling: 5 days on / 2 days off, or 8–12 week cycles at 2–3×/week. Avoid daily dosing beyond 3 weeks — receptor sensitivity falls.
peptides.mechanism: Next-generation Semax. Same ACTH(4–10) backbone for hippocampal BDNF upregulation and TrkB sensitization, plus an adamantyl group for deeper BBB penetration, enzymatic resistance, and 12–24 hour BDNF elevation (versus 30–60 minutes for standard Semax). Promotes neurogenesis. MC4R-related cycling is required to keep it working.
cautions: Morning only. Dosing after 1 PM commonly causes insomnia.
Start at 100 mcg. This is noticeably stimulating.
Do not run daily beyond about 3 weeks without a break — receptor sensitivity diminishes.
Cycling is part of efficacy, not just safety.
supplements: Lion’s Mane 500–1000 mg (NGF — different neurotrophin, same plasticity goal)
Alpha-GPC 300–600 mg (acetylcholine precursor for BDNF-driven demand)
Magnesium threonate 2 g (brain Mg for NMDA / LTP)
NAD+/NMN 500 mg fasted AM (ATP for structural brain changes)

peptides.name: Cerebrolysin
peptides.cardDescription: A porcine-derived peptide mixture used clinically in some countries and studied for stroke, brain injury, and cognitive decline. Think of it as a broad repair crew that imitates several of the brain’s own growth factors at once.
peptides.bottomLine: Supports neuronal survival, sprouting, and plasticity through multiple pathways.
peptides.dose: IM: 5 mL/day for 10–20 days. IV: 10–30 mL diluted in saline (clinical setting).
peptides.halfLife: Short plasma; effects accumulate over the course
peptides.timing: Morning preferred. IV requires a clinical setting.
peptides.cycling: 10–20 day courses, 1–2× per year. Not for daily ongoing use.
peptides.mechanism: A porcine-brain peptide hydrolysate. Low-molecular-weight fragments cross the blood–brain barrier where full-size BDNF, NGF, and GDNF cannot. Simultaneously mimics all three major neurotrophic factors: survival and plasticity (BDNF-like), cholinergic / peripheral repair (NGF-like), and dopaminergic / motor-neuron protection (GDNF-like). Promotes sprouting, neurogenesis, and synaptic plasticity; protects against excitotoxicity. Approved in 30+ countries for stroke, TBI, and dementia. Strongest clinical evidence of any cognitive peptide on this list.
cautions: IV belongs in a clinical setting.
Course-based only — not a daily take-home peptide.
Do not combine with MAO inhibitors.
Porcine-derived hydrolysate — relevant for allergy and sourcing questions.
supplements: Lion’s Mane 500–1000 mg (endogenous NGF to complement exogenous NGF-like fragments)

peptides.name: DSIP
peptides.cardDescription: A research peptide associated with delta, or slow-wave, sleep—the stage tied to physical repair, memory consolidation, and the largest natural growth-hormone pulse. Think of it as helping the brain spend more time in overnight maintenance mode.
peptides.bottomLine: Targets sleep depth and recovery rather than simply causing sedation.
peptides.timing: Bedtime, fasted. Not for chronic nightly use.
peptides.cycling: 2–4 week cycles, PRN. Not indefinitely every night.
peptides.mechanism: Isolated from rabbit cerebral venous blood during delta-sleep induction. Promotes delta (slow-wave) sleep — the stage of the largest natural GH pulse, glymphatic waste clearance, cellular repair, and memory consolidation. Normalizes cortisol/ACTH hypersecretion so those hormonal barriers to deep sleep come down. It is not a sedative. Deepens the exact sleep stage where CJC-1295 / Ipamorelin GH secretion peaks. Antioxidant during sleep.
cautions: Not a nightly-forever peptide. 2–4 week cycles or PRN.
Fasted at bedtime; food may blunt CNS delivery.
Not sedating — if cortisol is not the bottleneck, do not expect a knockout pill.
Start melatonin low if you stack it; more melatonin is not better.
supplements: Glycine 3 g bedtime in water (slow-wave sleep + lower core temperature)
Magnesium glycinate 400 mg bedtime (cortisol down + GABA-A)
Melatonin 0.5–3 mg bedtime, start low (sets the clock; DSIP deepens quality)
Ashwagandha 300–600 mg evening (the cortisol interference DSIP is already targeting)
L-theanine 200–400 mg bedtime (alpha-wave relaxed wakefulness → deep-sleep transition)

peptides.name: Thymosin Alpha-1
peptides.cardDescription: A thymic peptide used clinically in some countries and studied for coordinating innate and adaptive immune responses. Think of it as an immune-system coach that helps defense cells organize rather than simply pushing them harder.
peptides.bottomLine: Recalibrates immune coordination instead of acting like a generic booster.
peptides.dose: 1.6 mg SQ 2×/week standard. Up to 3.2 mg/week in clinical applications.
peptides.halfLife: ~2 hrs plasma; immune reprogramming lasts weeks
peptides.timing: Timing-independent.
peptides.cycling: 8–12 weeks on, 4 weeks off. Chronic protocols possible with supervision.
peptides.mechanism: A 28-amino-acid thymic peptide approved in 30+ countries (Zadaxin). Activates TLR9 on dendritic cells and lymphocytes — the innate sensor for microbial DNA — and bridges innate to adaptive immunity. Matures CD4+ helper and CD8+ cytotoxic T-cells, raises NK-cell killing, and restores Th1/Th2 balance (Th1 antiviral IFN-γ; excess Th2 is allergy/autoimmune). Mitochondrial connection: chronic immune dysregulation is a massive ATP drain. Normalizing it frees energy for everything else.
cautions: Chronic or higher-dose protocols belong under clinician supervision.
Vitamin D deficiency undercuts T-cell and NK function — the peptide cannot work in a D-empty immune system.
This is immune modulation, not a stimulant “immune boost.”
supplements: Vitamin D3/K2 10,000 IU + 200 mcg (required for T-cell / NK function)
Selenium 200 mcg as selenomethionine (GPx + thioredoxin reductase)
Glutathione liposomal 500–1000 mg (GSH depletion impairs T-cell and NK killing)
Methylated multi (B12/folate for T-cell DNA replication)
